rationale: Iteration 3 (kp 7.0, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05, 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.030 m, last_direction) was the best so far at 82.74, but every trial still ran off track. Its telemetry shows three things. (1) steering_oscillation on the oval rose to 0.25, above the 0.2 threshold that the Evaluator and my earlier plan set. The s-bend (0.12) and slalom (0.13) values are low, so the oval is where the jitter sits. (2) max_error is still 0.061 to 0.065, just over the 0.06 limit. (3) Line loss is down to 1 per run on the s-bend and slalom, and 1.65 on the oval. Progress is still poor (0.39 oval, 0.13 s-bend, 0.09 slalom). The Evaluator's conditional plan applies directly: when oscillation exceeds about 0.2 with kp 7.0, raise kd to 0.5 before cutting kp. Cutting kp would reduce the edge response that is currently keeping max_error near 0.06. I therefore change one variable: kd 0.4 to 0.5, with kp held at 7.0. Geometry, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05 and last_direction stay unchanged so the result is attributable to damping alone. Expected result: steering_oscillation on the oval falls back below about 0.2 while max_error stays near 0.06 or lower, and the oval line-loss count and progress hold or improve. Risk: kd 0.5 may slow the response to edge transients and lift max_error on the s-bend. Next measurements: steering_oscillation, max_error and line_loss_events per track, plus progress and rms_error. If oscillation is now low but max_error is still at or above 0.06, the next step is to widen the array to ±0.040 m and test kp near 8. If the s-bend and slalom keep one line loss at the same entries, the next step is to test line_loss search_left or search_right, choosing the side the failing bends favour. If progress is still below 1 with max_error under 0.06, raise base_speed toward 1.6.
